# Legacy workspace fixtures (P-0103 v3-25b / R-4.1)

Captured on-disk JSON artefacts for every historical
`STUDIO_FORMAT_VERSION`. The `tests/regression/test_legacy_workspace_fixtures.py`
suite loads each fixture and pins the read → migrate → write → reload
round-trip so a future schema bump cannot silently break a customer's
v0 / v1 / v2 workspace.

## Layout

| Path | Version | Provenance |
|---|---|---|
| `v0/meta.json` | v0 (pre-C-9, no `format_version` key) | Hand-built to the JobStore meta shape that existed before H-0081 landed |
| `v1/meta.json` | v1 (C-9 / H-0081, `format_version: 1`) | Hand-built to the same shape with the version sentinel |
| `v2/meta.json` | v2 (P-0099 v3-20a, `format_version: 2`) | Generated by the v3-20a runtime; includes the `paused` literal possibility |
| `v0/fit_result.json` | v0 fit_result | Hand-built skeleton matching the FitResult schema as of pre-C-9 |
| `v1/fit_result.json` | v1 fit_result | Same skeleton with `format_version: 1` prepended |
| `v2/fit_result.json` | v2 fit_result | Same skeleton with `format_version: 2` |

## Why hand-built rather than captured from real workspaces

Real customer workspaces include CSV paths, PII-shaped column names,
and trial-level checkpoint blobs that we cannot ship in the repo. The
shape under test is the **schema contract**, not the payload contents
— a hand-built skeleton with all canonical keys is sufficient to
detect a drop / rename / reshape. If a future migration legitimately
changes the schema, update the relevant fixture in the same PR.

## Adding a new version

When `STUDIO_FORMAT_VERSION` is bumped:

1. Add `tests/fixtures/legacy_workspaces/v<N>/meta.json` and
   `fit_result.json` with the on-disk shape that runtime emits.
2. The matrix in `test_legacy_workspace_fixtures.py` is parametrised
   on directory names — no test code change is required if the
   schema is identity-migratable.
3. If the migration is not identity, update `_EXPECTED_AFTER_MIGRATION`
   in the test file with the post-migration shape.
